title: Image Quality Assessment: From Error Visibility to Structural Similarity
role: CPU local luma SSIM map and timeline, with documented preprocessing and valid region.
limitations: Requires meaningful spatial/temporal correspondence.
Not a material, motion, semantic, or artistic acceptance metric.

title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Deep Features as a Perceptual Metric
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
role: Optional phase-matched frame/ROI perceptual distance; lower is more similar.
limitations: Image/patch similarity does not evaluate temporal event order or aesthetic direction.
Network, resize, crop, and weights affect comparability.

title: Image Quality Assessment: Unifying Structure and Texture Similarity
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
role: Optional full-image and reviewed material-ROI appearance distance.
limitations: Tolerance to texture resampling can hide exact pattern differences that matter for recreation.
Mild geometric tolerance must not erase framing errors.
Appearance features do not identify physical roughness, thickness, normals, transparency, or lighting correctness.

title: Two-Frame Motion Estimation Based on Polynomial Expansion
venue: Image Analysis, 13th Scandinavian Conference on Image Analysis (SCIA 2003), LNCS 2749
role: Optional CPU dense optical-flow estimator when OpenCV is already present.
limitations: No trained weights, but not currently installed according to implementation agent.
Two-frame displacement is not 3D motion, camera pose, or artistic fidelity.
code_license: OpenCV >=4.5 Apache-2.0; older versions BSD-3-Clause, per https://opencv.org/license/

title: RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow
role: Optional learned flow maps and within-stream motion descriptors, not a cross-film fidelity score.
limitations: Fast motion, occlusion, blur, textureless surfaces and stylization complicate correspondence.
Flow measures projected image motion, not volume, physical causality or emotion.

title: TransNet V2: An effective deep network architecture for fast shot transition detection
role: Optional per-frame transition probability and proposed shot boundaries for human verification.
limitations: False detections and misses remain possible.
Do not relabel a coarse frame-difference detector as TransNet.
Map frame-index results to actual source PTS; validate flashes/fades/rapid cuts.

title: VBench: Comprehensive Benchmark Suite for Video Generative Models
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
role: Adopt disentangled dashboard dimensions and human checks, not official aggregate score or numerical claims.
limitations: Model/quality/condition evaluation is not paired full-reference reconstruction validation.
A stable frozen clip can still omit the reference action.
Current repository includes multiple VBench generations; pin exact method/version if later enabled.

title: Towards Accurate Generative Models of Video: A New Metric & Challenges
role: Do not implement as a single-reference/candidate acceptance score.
limitations: Compares distributions of video embeddings; sample size affects estimates.
One pair cannot support the intended distribution/covariance estimation.
Overlapping windows are correlated and do not turn one film into a validated independent benchmark dataset.
A distribution match is not proof of paired event timing, framing, material, or shot fidelity.

title: Beat Tracking by Dynamic Programming
role: Plot onset envelope and multiple tempo hypotheses, including half/double-tempo ambiguity. If only spectral flux/autocorrelation are implemented, label Ellis-inspired baseline, not an implementation of the full DP tracker.
limitations: Beat/onset/BPM do not determine mood or musical suitability.
Global-tempo assumption and metrical ambiguity limit inference.
Short, quiet, non-pulsed, or SFX-dominant excerpts may have no defensible beat estimate.

title: Large-Scale Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining with Feature Fusion and Keyword-to-Caption Augmentation
role: Optional time-windowed reference/candidate audio embedding distance and descriptive prompt retrieval. Store checkpoint identity, preprocessing, prompt set, crop length, and retrieval margin.
limitations: Cosine similarity is an embedding proxy, not probability of good music or emotional correctness.
Prompt wording and checkpoint training domain can influence comparisons.
No frame-accurate synchronization or stereo object tracking claim follows from audio-text similarity.

title: Language-Guided Music Recommendation for Video via Prompt Analogies
role: Create an explicit music brief describing intended role, instrumentation, mood, density, and changes, then compare candidates with the same visual segment. Treat text labels as requirements/evidence, not fabricated hearing.
limitations: Retrieval on music-video data is not a calibrated soundtrack-acceptance metric for MotionStudio animation.
Does not establish that a retrieved track is tasteful or that SFX timing is correct.
No model implementation or code availability should be implied by adopting the interface idea.

title: Synchformer: Efficient Synchronization from Sparse Cues
role: Optional offset-hypothesis plot plus synchronizability/abstention. Cross-check model proposals against source frames and PCM events. Use sparse-cue model, not speech-only SyncNet, for general events.
limitations: Natural-video training does not certify stylized animation or intentionally designed anticipatory sound.
Global offset is not a per-SFX onset adjudicator or aesthetic score.
Official example uses positive offset for early audio; MotionStudio audio-minus-visual convention uses positive for late audio. Adapter must convert and test both signs.
0.64-second segment processing is not a claim of frame-level timing accuracy.

title: AI Choreographer: Music Conditioned 3D Dance Generation with AIST++
role: Display event-to-beat distances for explicitly selected rhythm-coupled moments, and show whether the reference itself is on-beat or intentionally off-beat.
limitations: Designed for 3D human dance, not every shape motion, camera cut, or sound effect.
Original sigma=3 frames at 60 fps must not become a universal 3-frame threshold; use seconds and domain-specific tolerances.
Do not demand a visual event on every music beat; original metric itself is unidirectional.
Static holds and sparse/offbeat motion must remain valid where intentional.

title: Dynamic Programming Algorithm Optimization for Spoken Word Recognition
venue: IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
role: Optional inspectable constrained alignment of comparable event/onset or embedding sequences. Preserve raw PTS view and report warp path/local stretch separately.
limitations: Original validation concerns spoken words, not animation fidelity.
Warping can conceal wrong motion timing or missing events.
Use a bounded band, monotonic anchors, explicit unmatched events, and raw versus aligned results; never silently optimize away the defect being evaluated.

title: Fréchet Audio Distance: A Reference-Free Metric for Evaluating Music Enhancement Algorithms
role: Reserve for a later, fixed-corpus aggregate study. Do not display FAD as a reference-recreation pair score.
limitations: Reference-free means no paired clean target, not no background reference distribution.
One reference clip versus one candidate clip is not the paper's evaluation protocol.
Distribution proximity does not establish matching mood, beat phase, arrangement, SFX identity, or AV synchronization.

title: Adapting Frechet Audio Distance for Generative Music Evaluation
role: If a future corpus-level dashboard adds FAD, log embedding/checkpoint, reference corpus, excerpt duration, sample count, and uncertainty. Keep soundtrack-fit and synchronization evidence separate.
limitations: Per-song FAD exists, so 'FAD can never score a song' is inaccurate; it is still not a paired reference-fidelity measure.
The listening study evaluates acoustic/musical quality, not prompt adherence or fit to a specific visual.
Genre imbalance can shift results; low FAD is not universally better for an intentionally unusual soundtrack.
